title: Leave room for a steered wheel inside a fender
applicability: Use when a road wheel swings into a fender, wheel arch, bumper or bodywork. Use the actual wheel and tire dimensions and the intended steering axis and range.
aliases: wheel arch hits tire when turning
steps: Build a steering-side test rig before enclosing the whole axle. Attach the actual wheel and tire (4624c01 here) to the moving carrier. Mount a representative fender edge to the fixed chassis.
Check the centered wheel and sample both steering locks and angles between. If suspension is also modeled, evaluate steering at multiple ride heights with the same fender geometry.

Inspect the specific tire/fender sample. The example moves the fender corner one stud outward while keeping the steering travel. Compare that packaging choice with moving the pivot, which also changes the location of the tire throughout the range.
expected: At 0° the wheel clears. The wheel and fender collide at +45° in the original rig. Moving the fender one stud clears all five samples from −45° to +45°.

sources.author: Carlos Antelo
sources.title: Steerable Technic front axle study
sources.adaptation: Reference only. The documented parent/steering layout inspired separating fixed bodywork from the moving wheel. The fixture is an original single-wheel clearance rig. The BrickWright guidance and example are original.
